title: Wes Anderson needs his “StarDust Memories” moment

commenti.body:
With all due respect, your chronology is off. You argue that *Stardust Memories* represents the end of Woody Allen's early style and the beginning of "a different path which lead eventually to Annie Hall and Manhattan. And so on so forth."

*Stardust Memories* (1980) actually came out **after** *Annie Hall* (1977) and *Manhattan* (1979). To say that it opened up a creative path that led to those two films is simply anachronistic. 

And, of course, *Stardust Memories* is not the first example of the self-reflexive, pseudo-autobiographical auteur film. *All That Jazz* came out the year before, and both films clearly take influence from *8 1/2*. 

Furthermore, opinions on the film itself vary greatly but I think one could read *Asteroid City* as the equivalent in Wes Anderson's filmography -- his self-reflexive film about filmmaking, a film in some sense about its own artifice.

Sure, but Stardust came out after Annie Hall and Manhattan to massive success (including Best Director/Picture) . Those are what set the stage for his ‘80s run of more serious comedies.

Wes Anderson makes what he makes. There’s no movie in the world like his, and they are nearly always enjoyable. Should he eventually turn down the dial a bit? Not a bad idea

Nobody else makes wes anderson films. Just like nobody else makes terrence malick films. I’m not a huge wes anderson fan but just because his style is distinct and consistent doesn’t mean he needs to change it up. 

I want these auteurs to make whatever they want. I find this kind of criticism sad when it’s targeted at the few people who actually have distinct filmographies.
